vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: compound-eng-file-todos
Version: 2.55.0

The skill bundle provides a structured framework for file-based task management using Markdown files in a dedicated 'todos/' directory. It includes templates, naming conventions, and standard bash commands (grep, ls, mv, awk) for an agent to manage task lifecycles, dependencies, and work logs. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution was found; all instructions and scripts are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of project tracking.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its described purpose: it is an instruction-only, file-based todo management guide that operates on a todos/ directory and requests no credentials or installs.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the instructions: everything centers on creating, triaging, and managing markdown todo files in a todos/ directory. The SKILL.md mentions integrations (PR comments, gh CLI, slash commands) but the skill does not declare or require GitHub credentials or CLI binaries — this is a reasonable omission for an instruction-only skill but worth noting if you plan to use those integrations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to reading, creating, renaming, and searching markdown files under todos/ and to using the provided template and workflow docs. The commands in the references (ls, grep, mv, awk, basic shell tests) are standard CLI operations and do not reference unrelated system paths, secrets, or external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files — this is an instruction-only skill, so nothing is downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate. If you later use the mentioned GitHub/PR integrations in practice, those will require separate credentials (e.g., GH_TOKEN) and CLI tools; the skill does not claim or request those.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: disable-model-invocation is set to true in the skill metadata, so the skill will not be autonomously invoked by the model. It does not request always:true or any special persistent privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an instruction set for managing markdown todos in a todos/ directory and does not install code or ask for secrets. Before using it: ensure your repository has (or will have) a dedicated todos/ folder and that you are comfortable with an agent or user running the listed shell commands (ls, grep, mv, etc.) which will read and rename files there. If you plan to integrate with GitHub PRs or use the gh CLI, set up credentials and the CLI separately and restrict those tokens appropriately — the skill itself does not request or manage those credentials. Finally, confirm that no sensitive data will be stored in todos/ files, since they are plain text and intended to be read/edited by humans and tools.
